audit.whatIsWrong: Three sources give three different level charts. Page (both layers agree): Skill/Sion/Sion/Skill/Skill/Sion/Sion. Packet: Skill/Skill/Sion/Skill/Skill/Sion/Skill. Mirror summary: Garen through first item, Sion at two-plus items.
audit.why: The page's two layers at least agree with each other, so nothing renders split. The mirror's version — a Garen sweep of six rows — is hard to square with a 49.96% win rate over 4922 games, and I only have its summary, not its rows. Guessing here would either fight the mirror or contradict the data.
audit.corrected: Chart left untouched; question raised for the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage's cooldown is stated as '21 seconds at rank 1' in whys[3] and again in mid. It is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12. Demacian Justice is told to be tracked with no number given.
audit.why: Real numbers are what make the 'trade in the gap' advice usable — and a wrong one is worse than none. R is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: 22s for Courage in both places; 120s stated for Demacian Justice at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the matchup says Decisive Strike breaks slows. The page builds its whole trade pattern on E-slow into charged Q, and Garen's Q undoes the slow half of that for free on an 8s cooldown.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him.' Roar of the Slayer's slow is therefore not a lockdown against Garen — only the armour shred survives. Q is also an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[0] now leads with the slow-break and names the 8s cooldown.

audit.why: Courage at 22s rank 1 is genuinely the punishable window and the page is built around it; only the number was wrong.

edits.before: Garen's passive regen hasn't started yet and his Courage W is on a long cooldown at rank 1 — farm safely and deny him a free Q silence to open the trade.
edits.after: Perseverance only regenerates while he is untouched and Courage is 22s at rank 1 — chip him with autos to switch the regen off and deny the free Q silence.

edits.before: Garen can passive-regen poke you with silencing Qs and disengage; both kits are online but neither has a decisive spike, so track Courage W and only engage in that 21-second gap.
edits.after: Garen pokes with silencing Qs and then disengages to regen; neither kit has a decisive spike here, so track Courage (22s at rank 1) and only engage inside that gap.

edits.before: Open with a silencing Q to cancel your charged Q cast, then spin E through you
edits.after: Break your E slow with Decisive Strike (8s), silence you, then spin E through you

edits.before: Garen's R becomes a genuine execute threat when you're at half HP — never give him a low-HP target, and track Demacian Justice cooldown before you all-in.
edits.after: Demacian Justice is true damage on a 120s cooldown at rank 1 — stay above the execute line, and all-in only in the window after he has spent it.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the quietest stretch for you — Garen can play passive-regen denial, stepping up only when his Q silence is ready, and you lack the mobility to force a fight he doesn't want. Track his Courage W cooldown (21 seconds at rank 1 — a very long gap) and only charge your Q when that window is open. At level 6 you gain Unstoppable Onslaught for all-in threat and the ability to deny his regen reset by chasing him to his turret, but his Demacian Justice now becomes a real deterrent — never give him a sub-40% HP target or he can execute through your W-shield. Trade when he's above 60% HP and your R is up so his execute math doesn't pencil out.

notes: UNVERIFIED and deliberately left in place, matching the mirror's decision: five fields (whys[2], early, mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0]) assume Garen's Q silence cancels an in-progress Decimating Smash charge. Riot's text does not call the charge a channel and the kit carries no channel flag, so silence-cancels-charge is not answerable from kit data. I rewrote wants.foe[0] around the slow-break instead of the cancel, which is verifiable, and left the other four alone. Courage also grants brief tenacity on activation, which shortens your Q stun if he pops it on reaction — the page mentions tenacity only in the late paragraph.
